beats.headline: Races, classes and a manager in a tuxedo
beats.text: Class selection, on the way in. Donut stays a cat, as she always said she would, and on Odette's advice she takes Former Child Actor, a class that lets her try on a new one at every level. She and Odette also arrange, as an accident that is not one, for Mordecai to become her manager, which means he goes where she goes. He will forgive Donut. Carl, no. Carl takes Primal, the race nobody alive remembers the look of, and a class nobody has taken before, Compensated Anarchist: a trap-making, bomb-making social-media dynamo. The floor above collapses mid-selection, leaving just over seven hundred thousand crawlers and eight days on the clock. The Over City is a ruin built on a ruin, full of printed NPCs whose memories are rewritten every time they respawn, guarded by level-75 swordsmen, and signposted by rocks that grow holographic signs when you look at them. Mordecai is an incubus in a tuxedo now, and on his first night in an Over City pub he learns that an incubus's weakness is alcohol. A lemur throws a knife, a quest called The Show Must Go On arrives with trumpets, and Donut drops an eleven-foot stilt clown so Carl can land on it. Their Earth boxes bring Donut a cat tree and a candle, and Carl a Home Depot cactus and eighteen L'Amour westerns like the ones his father kept. His hands shake and he does not know why.

beats.headline: Signet, a bear, and the man who became a vine
beats.text: Scouting Grimaldi's Traveling Circus at dusk, they run into the woman from its posters: Tsarina Signet, half naiad, half elf, an Elite with a charisma past a hundred and tattoos that swim. Carl breaks his own pinky to shake off the spell. She needs a sacrifice's blood to raise her paper army, and when Carl breaks his word to her she puts Donut into a magical sleep called Water Lily and keeps her as the price. Carl earns her back the hard way. He kills Heather the Bear, a clown-ridden circus veteran on roller skates, and his lottery ticket casts custard instead of fireball, which heals the parasites out of her and leaves an old bear asking for it to be over. Signet's army breaks the circus defenders but cannot break the big top. Inside it waits Ringmaster Grimaldi: the dwarf who raised Signet, now a Pestiferous Vine, a level-85 city boss and an Elite at once. No crawler this season has faced a city boss and lived. Carl sits in the bleachers, poisons himself, and bleeds on the roots. Then he makes a deal with the producers of Signet's own show, Vengeance of the Daughter: he will play his part in it on the sixth floor if they let tonight go his way. He reads Wisp Armor, eats a cone of worms from a strongman so the vine can speak in his head, and talks Grimaldi into lifting Signet's banishment. She walks into the tent.

beats.headline: Family, a pharmacist, and a woman nobody helped
beats.text: Carl gets back to find Donut still asleep and Mongo standing over her in a ring of dead street urchins, full of spikes. With Mongo curled on his lap and the cat breathing on his neck, Carl counts who he has left in the world, and it is everyone in the room. This is my family. The circus vanishes by morning and a stairwell sits where it stood. A Scroll of Upgrade improves Carl's boxers enormously and adds Freeballing, which permits one layer over the crotch, so trousers are now off the table for good. Donut's charisma is past seventy; they build a playbook of named plays, and the Boomy Boy is a clockwork Mongo with dynamite in each hand. In a pub an old orc called GumGum asks for help and Mordecai tells her to go away. Women are being found in the alleys every morning with the blood drained out of them. The next night GumGum is on the ground with her chest torn open, three flying heads trailing their own organs above her, and in her pocket is a letter in necroscript. Mordecai reads the squiggles: a lich problem. Donut decides they are finishing GumGum's quest because GumGum died for it. Meanwhile the Desperado Club opens to them: Clarabelle on the door, Quint the pharmacist, Pustule and her hob-lobbers, and news that Lucia Mar has already been thrown out. The fan boxes deliver a photograph of Bea on her ex's lap, and a jai-alai scoop that finally makes a weapon out of Carl's arm.

beats.headline: Danger Zone
beats.text: Carl throws a corpse on Miss Quill's desk as evidence, waves a pass that keeps the swordsmen off him, and while she is picking her beanbag figures up off the floor he fixes her shelf. It is hollow, and he fills it with dynamite. An ambush of city elves and shambling berserkers ends with Carl blind, jumping into a swimming pool full of dead boss, and waking up on a roof. Then comes Danger Zone, a chat show on a boat with Ripper Wonton hosting, a comedian Donut renames Butler, a Naga pop star called Manasa, Princess D'nadia, and Hekla. When the host asks about unrest in the Skull Empire, Carl tells the story of the frog in the pot: if it used to be okay and it isn't any more, kick them out. Barely two minutes pass before the Empire answers with a pulse from Prince Stalwart's yacht, aimed at Carl and Donut's trailer. Manasa had swapped trailers with them. The Valtay, whose worm was driving her dead body, destroy the yacht in return, with the queen consort and the disgraced Maestro rumoured aboard. Mordecai makes a new rule: nobody outside the dungeon gets mentioned again. Back on the ground, elves at a temple proclaim Donut the Oak Fell, She Who Ends, because of an anklet off a dead crawler; Mongo eats a dwarf boy's arm; the temple burns. Hekla asks them to take Katia Grim, a doppelgänger who is ten levels behind, and they do. They feed the lich's letter to a pair of clockwork Mongos as bait and blow Miss Quill's building from a roof away.

beats.headline: The Fools Who Broke the Glass
beats.text: Miss Quill dies with her shelves, and Carl is suddenly magistrate of the town. Inside they find the real Featherfall, long dead and mummified in a dreamcatcher of bone, and a meat locker of hanging women who wake up as krasue. The lottery ticket finally lands on fireball. Burgundy, one of the women, lives long enough to explain: Quill ran the town all along, and across the street is her husband, Remex. Remex is not a lich and not a boss. He is a Soul Leech Capacitor, a dead man pulled back to feed his wife the power of the town's soul crystal for an ancient spell called The Final War, and with Quill dead the spell is coming apart. The quest that drops on every crawler within forty-five square kilometres is short: don't die. Carl could run. Instead he closes a Sheol Glass Reaper Case around the cracking gem and puts it in his inventory, where it becomes Carl's Doomsday Scenario: a bomb big enough to flatten a city, which goes off the moment it comes out. Four shocks tear through the district. Magic is stripped from gear, weapons fire where they hang, a ranger dies when his own arrows go off in his quiver, and Donut's crown crumbles to dust on her head, though the succession stays. Carl runs east in a jacket and nothing else, Katia bursts through a wall, and at the bottom of the stairs she presses the detonator. The explosion saves thousands and earns eighty-three crawlers a Celestial box. Borant burns its one veto of the season to void them, a moment after Quan Ch has opened his. On Odette's couch the leaderboard goes up. It is a list of bounties: Lucia Mar first, Hekla second, Carl sixth, Donut seventh.
